entities.title: num.rs names the old diagnostic code range
entities.summary: The module documentation of num.rs says an overflow is reported as unsupported with diagnostic range; since 0.3.0 the code is implementation-limit.
entities.expected: The comment names the code the library reports: implementation-limit (model.rs range_err; CHANGELOG 0.3.0 renamed range to implementation-limit).
entities.observed: "An overflow gives None, which the operations report as unsupported (diagnostic range) rather than wrapping or rounding."

entities.title: Two copies of the leap-year and month-length rules
entities.summary: lib.rs and num.rs each define is_leap and days_in_month, and the two days_in_month differ for months outside 1 to 12.
entities.details: lib.rs's public `days_in_month(year, month) -> Option<u32>` answers None for a month outside 1 to 12; num.rs's crate-internal `days_in_month(year, month) -> u32` answers 28 or 29 for it (its last match arm). lib.rs uses its own copy in check_civil; model.rs, iso.rs and ops.rs use num.rs's, after checking the month.
entities.compromise: The public helpers in lib.rs were kept beside the crate-internal ones in num.rs instead of one calling the other.
entities.cost: A fix to the calendar rules has to be made twice, and a caller of num::days_in_month that skips the month check gets a plausible wrong answer.

origin.description: is_leap and days_in_month at the end of lib.rs, and the same names in num.rs.
